name: Jeshua
overview: Jeshua was a male Levite who served as the ninth-chosen priest among the twenty-four priestly courses established for temple service. He belonged to the line of Eleazar, one of the sons of Aaron, which positioned him within the priestly lineage responsible for maintaining the worship and sacrifices in Israel. His role as a priest highlights his important function in the religious life of ancient Israel.
namesAndTitles: The name Jeshua means 'YHWH saves,' reflecting a theologically rich meaning tied to God's saving power. This proper name is recorded in 1 Chronicles 24:11 and underscores the divine association embedded in his identity.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture identifies Jeshua as a descendant of Eleazar, situating him within that priestly family line. Additionally, he is connected as a descendant of Jedaiah, as inferred from Ezra 2:36. Beyond these ancestral links, no further family relationships are explicitly recorded in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Jeshua's significance lies in his appointment as the ninth priestly course among the twenty-four divisions established to organize temple service. Being from the line of Eleazar, he represents continuity in the priestly heritage that was vital to Israel's worship system. His role reflects God's provision for orderly and sustained priestly ministry in the post-exilic period, as detailed in 1 Chronicles and Ezra.
